name: Kawah Ijen, East Java, Indonesia

process.text: Acid-sulfate alteration: a crater lake with a pH below 0.3 alters the volcanic rock around it.

links.text: Gale's lake mudstones hold jarosite, an iron sulfate, measured by Curiosity.

process.differs: Kawah Ijen is an active, hot, wet system today. Gale's lake is ancient and long dry.

name: Mount Tambora caldera, Sumbawa, Indonesia
source: Smithsonian GVP volcano 264040 (the 1815 eruption 'formed a 6-km-wide, 1250-m-deep caldera'); position: centre of the caldera rim traced on the Copernicus DEM GLO-30 elevation model
note: Proposed by a team member as an Earth counterpart to a deep polar crater such as Shackleton. No source links it to planetary research: the analog idea is SBATS's own, so analogFor is empty. Shackleton is 21 km wide and 4.1 km deep (Zuber et al. 2012, Nature), about three times Tambora in both directions: see validation/sites/FINDINGS.md.

process.text: Caldera collapse: the 1815 eruption left a caldera 6 km wide and 1,250 m deep.

links.text: Shackleton is a crater 21 km wide and 4.1 km deep with steep walls.

process.differs: Shackleton is an impact crater; Tambora collapsed after an eruption. The shapes are alike, the process is not, and Tambora is about a third of the size.
